correctness.rationale: In the infectious equation, every recovered-stage term is a product R_k times I. At S=N, I=0 and all R_k=0, its full first derivative is zero, whereas the susceptible infection term contributes beta(t) and recovery plus mortality contributes minus gamma plus mu. The exact scalar variational equation therefore has one-period multiplier equal to the exponential of the integral of beta(t) minus gamma plus mu. The cosine forcing has mean beta_0/2, giving the stated strict stability, neutrality and instability boundary. The case-study threshold 2.0003244 and the source's three fitted beta amplitudes were independently recomputed; the numerical checker only corroborates this analytic Jacobian argument.

originality.rationale: The 2025 seasonal SIRn paper itself prints a time-dependent reproduction number obtained by averaging the susceptible and recovered-stage transmission rates, while its own differential equations show that recovered-stage reinfection terms are bilinear in a recovered perturbation and the infectious perturbation. No correction or erratum resolving this discrepancy was found in targeted searches. General periodic epidemic threshold literature supports linearized/Floquet invasion analysis, but the source-specific corrected threshold and the diagnosis of Eq. 19 were not located elsewhere.
residual_risks: A non-indexed author note or future correction could independently make the same source-specific observation.

source_inspections.evidence: Eq. 1 makes each recovered reinfection contribution proportional to R_k times I, while Eq. 19 averages their beta_k coefficients into the stated reproduction number even though every R_k is zero at the disease-free state.
source_inspections.material_read: The open full primary article was inspected around the model system, recovered-stage rate definition, sinusoidal forcing and Eq. 19 reproduction-number discussion.
source_inspections.title: Mathematical Modeling of Influenza Dynamics: Integrating Seasonality and Gradual Waning Immunity
source_inspections.trigger: Defining primary source containing both the model equations and the disputed Eq. 19.

value.rationale: A basic reproduction or invasion threshold is a central interpretive quantity of an epidemic model. Showing from the published equations that a printed recovered-class average cannot be that threshold, and supplying the exact corrected Floquet boundary for the article's case study, is a substantively motivated correction rather than a cosmetic normalization check.
residual_risks: A non-indexed author note or future correction could independently make the same source-specific observation.

final_claim: For the published seasonal SIRn equations at the fully susceptible disease-free state, recovered-stage reinfection terms do not enter first-order invasion; the exact sinusoidal one-period threshold is beta_0 equal to twice gamma plus mu, independent of the recovered-stage number and susceptibility profile, so the class-averaged quantity printed in Eq. 19 is not the disease-free invasion threshold.
scientific_limitations: A non-indexed author note or future correction could independently make the same source-specific observation.
The result is local to disease-free invasion and does not establish nonlinear persistence, global extinction or correctness of the fitted trajectories themselves.
